transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46m
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Sierra Head of AI), Tom Han (Infra), Aaliyah Brooks (PM)

Summary (auto): Quick econ review, touched on batching, caching, and security. Decided tests and pricing spreadsheet updates.

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, Priya, Tom, Aaliyah. We wanted to run through the pilot economics and show the latest numbers Marco pulled from the pilot run.
[00:18] Priya Desai: Yeah thanks Lena, trying to keep this tight, we have leadership check-in next week so want concrete numbers on tokens per dollar and any risks.
[00:30] Marco Ruiz: Great, first slide, quick numbers: baseline hosted run (gpt-ish open model, q4_8bit) averaged about 850 tokens/sec and cost roughly $0.009 per 1k tokens, which yields about 94 tokens/sec per dollar in the current test config. That includes prefix caching disabled for that route.
[01:02] Tom Han: Wait 850 tokens/sec on which instance? Like a single GPU?
[01:08] Marco Ruiz: Single V100-like equivalent in our Dedicated sim — but for hosted it's multi-tenant cyl. The pilot used a 1xA10/16GB-ish profile; numbers are synthetic to match your reqs. Speech in transcript may mix labels, sorry.
[01:28] Aaliyah Brooks: We're primarily worried about the patient-summary route — it's heavy on context and long histories, so tokens per request blow up quickly. Any cache wins there?
[01:42] Marco Ruiz: Yes, we ran a prefix caching pass for the last 48 hours on a subset — it saved about 37% of total generated tokens for the patient-summary route where ~60% of requests had overlapping history. That bumped tokens/sec per dollar up to about 129 tokens/sec/$ in the cached run.
[02:10] Priya Desai: 37% is big. Is that KV cache or full prefix? Which TTL?
[02:18] Marco Ruiz: It's prefix+KV keyed on patient_id+last_3_msgs; TTL was set to 30 minutes for the test. If you increase the TTL to 4 hours we saw marginal additional savings but risk staleness for some workflows.
[02:40] Lena Park: Tradeoff note: longer TTL -> more token savings but more chance of stale sensitive state; depends on your data freshness SLA.
[02:52] Tom Han: From infra side, we need to know if any caching requires KMS access or has PII implications. We can't keep patient PHI in a shared cache, so we'd want VPC/private deployment for those keys.
[03:08] Marco Ruiz: Good point — for PHI we recommend Redwood Private with encrypted KV, and we support customer-side KMS. That avoids storing decrypted content in shared infra. We'll include a config example.
[03:24] Priya Desai: Okay. On batching — we saw batch sizes of 4 reduce CPU overhead but increased tail latency. Can you quantify that?
[03:35] Marco Ruiz: In our tests, synchronous batching with a batch size cap of 8 improved throughput by ~30% at the cost of tail p95 latency going from ~120ms to ~240ms for those routes. If low-latency SLAs are critical, you want smaller batch caps or async background batching with latency SLOs.
[04:00] Aaliyah Brooks: For patient summaries we need p95 < 300ms ideally. So 240ms p95 might be OK, but 120 to 240 is a big change. Is that consistent?
[04:12] Marco Ruiz: It's workload dependent — if sequences are long batching helps amortize KV cache hits but increases serialization and scheduling delay. We recommend a dynamic batch policy: prioritize low-latency for flagged user interactions, use larger batch windows for background summarization.
[04:33] Priya Desai: Can Redwood route by policy? E.g., route real-time UI calls to low-latency pool and background jobs to dedicated cheap pool?
[04:42] Lena Park: Yes, smart routing supports policy-based routing. You can pin routes to dedicated pools, set SLO-based preferences, and fallback to hosted if capacity's constrained. We'll share an example routing policy per route.
[04:56] Tom Han: On cost modeling, we need dedicated vs hosted break-even. What assumptions did you use?
[05:05] Marco Ruiz: We modeled three scenarios: light load (50 qps), steady (200 qps), heavy (600 qps). For each we included GPU amortization, support costs, and caching savings. In steady-state the dedicated pool becomes cheaper past ~120 qps after we include reserved capacity discounts. We'll attach the spreadsheet.
[05:28] Priya Desai: Where's the spreadsheet link?
[05:31] Lena Park: I'll drop the link in the notes — "sierra-pilot-pricing-v2.xlsx" (shared). Marco, you already updated the tokens/sec sheet?
[05:40] Marco Ruiz: Yep I added a tab with token/sec/$ and separate rows for cached vs uncached traffic, plus quantized model variants q4_8bit vs q2_k. q2_k traded off smaller model size for some quality and got about 1.7x tokens/sec but produced slight regression on extraction accuracy in our eval set.
[06:05] Aaliyah Brooks: That accuracy regression — do we have specific numbers? If the summary misses key meds we can't accept it.
[06:12] Marco Ruiz: On our validation prompts, q4_8bit F1 was 0.92 on entity extraction, q2_k dropped to 0.88. So there's a measurable gap. We can try hybrid: quantize only encoder layers or use mixed precision. That often captures most perf gains with smaller quality loss.
[06:36] Priya Desai: Any other knobs? Temperature, sampling? Probably less relevant for extraction tasks.
[06:43] Marco Ruiz: Right, for deterministic extraction we recommend greedy or low-temp sampling and focus on model variant and caching. Also you can use rerankers for edge cases — that adds cost but keeps quality.
[06:55] Tom Han: About security — SOC2 and SSO — what docs can you share?
[06:59] Lena Park: We have SOC2 Type II doc, ISO notice, and an SSO/SAML integration guide. I'll push those to the shared folder. Also config examples for KMS.
[07:12] Priya Desai: Data residency — we need EU only for cardiac data. Can Redwood pin workloads to eu-central?
[07:18] Marco Ruiz: Yes, we support region pinning and private deployment options. For PHI we'd recommend Private in your VPC in eu-central and bring-your-own-KMS.
[07:29] Aaliyah Brooks: Back to the numbers — you mentioned token/sec per dollar moving from 94 to 129 with caching. How robust is that? 37% is from subset; is it representative?
[07:40] Marco Ruiz: We saw variance by route — patient-summary more benefit because of long histories. In high-cardinality routes savings are lower (~10-12%). We'll run the full 24h pass to get steadier metrics across traffic patterns.
[08:00] Priya Desai: Okay let's prioritize the patient-summary route test.
[08:05] Marco Ruiz: We'll run with the same traffic mix you've been replaying — 30% long-history sessions, 70% short ones. We'll enable prefix caching TTL 30m and also test TTL 4h in a small bucket to see risk.
[08:20] Lena Park: Logistics — Marco will upload logs and the token accounting. We'll normalize to tokens per sec per dollar using your reserved pricing assumption.
[08:29] Tom Han: One more infra ask: can we get sample configs for Redis-backed KV cache vs in-memory? We need to see ops impact.
[08:37] Marco Ruiz: Sure — we'll include both config samples and ops notes. Redis-backed persists across restarts but has extra network latency; in-memory is fastest but less durable. For your workload we recommend redis with local caching layer.
[08:53] Priya Desai: Cool. Any blockers from Redwood side?
[08:57] Marco Ruiz: No blockers. We need final confirmation on data residency and whether you want private deployment to test PHI routes.
[09:06] Priya Desai: I'll confirm by Monday.
[09:09] Lena Park: Great. Next meeting — same time next week? We'll do a short follow-up after the 24h results.
[09:15] Aaliyah Brooks: Works for us.
[09:17] Lena Park: Recap of next steps: Marco run 24h test; Lena send pricing spreadsheet and security docs; Priya confirm EU residency; schedule dedicated-run if metrics are good.
[09:29] Priya Desai: Thanks everyone.
[09:32] Marco Ruiz: Thanks, bye.
[09:33] Lena Park: Bye.

Notes / Attachments referenced:
- sierra-pilot-pricing-v2.xlsx (pricing model, tokens/sec tab)
- short-demo-deck.pdf (routing & caching options)
- security-pack.zip (SOC2, SAML guide, KMS integration example)
